extracted.intended_audience: interested persons, stakeholders, and regulated parties wishing to submit comments on proposed California regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public and stakeholders on how to find, submit, and craft effective written and oral comments under the California Administrative Procedure Act (APA) during rulemaking. Covers procedural deadlines, where notices are published, and substantive strategies to maximize impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum comment period length
rubrics_metrics.description: The California APA requires an agency to provide for a minimum forty-five day written comment period wherein interested persons can submit written comments. This Public Comment Period begins when the Notice of Proposed Action (NOPA) is published in the Notice Register and ends when specified in the NOPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure any written comment is submitted within the 45-day minimum period (or the period specified in the NOPA). Use the Notice Register publication date as the start date for counting days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where NOPAs and ISORs are published
rubrics_metrics.description: All NOPAs are published in the California Regulatory Notice Register (Notice Register), which is issued every Friday. The agency must also mail the notice to those persons who have requested notice of regulatory actions, and post the notice and Initial Statement of Reasons on the agency's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate proposed rulemakings by checking the weekly Notice Register, subscribing/requesting notice from agencies, and reviewing the agency's website for the NOPA and Initial Statement of Reasons (ISOR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written comments are accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons or parties may submit written comments directly to the agency about the proposed rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use written comments to present factual arguments, cite authority, and request specific agency responses in the Final Statement of Reasons (FSOR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing: acceptance of written and oral comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must accept both written and oral comments at the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hearing is scheduled, prepare to present both written submissions and oral testimony; oral comments entered at the hearing become part of the rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to request a hearing (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency does not schedule a public hearing, any interested person can make a request for a hearing. The request must be made in writing within 15 days of the close of the written comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no hearing is scheduled but you want one, submit a written hearing request within 15 days after the written comment period closes to preserve the right to a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must respond to relevant comments
rubrics_metrics.description: California's APA has a stronger requirement than federal: agencies must respond to 'relevant' comments specifically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame comments so they are clearly ‘relevant’ (directed at the proposed regulations or procedures followed) to increase the likelihood of a specific agency response in the FSOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the specific authority and reference statutes cited in the NOPA
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximize impact: Address the specific authority and reference statutes cited in the NOPA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie your comment to the statutory or regulatory authority the agency cites; explain why the agency's claimed authority does or does not support the proposed regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the Initial Statement of Reasons (ISOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximize impact: Engage with the Initial Statement of Reasons (ISOR)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically analyze and respond to the ISOR's factual and legal bases — challenge assumptions, point out missing analysis, or supply contrary evidence and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and note alternatives required by Government Code §11346.2(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximize impact: Note alternatives the agency must consider per Government Code §11346.2(b)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose feasible regulatory alternatives or point out alternatives the agency failed to consider to force the agency to address alternatives in the FSOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the agency's economic impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximize impact: Address the agency's economic impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge or supplement the economic analysis with data, methodology critiques, or alternative economic assumptions to show the analysis is incomplete or flawed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite the specific California Code of Regulations sections being amended
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximize impact: Cite to specific California Code of Regulations sections being amended
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference exact CCR section numbers and proposed regulatory text so the agency can readily identify what your comment targets and respond in kind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand the Final Statement of Reasons (FSOR) address your specific points
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximize impact: Demand the Final Statement of Reasons address your specific points
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request explicit responses in the FSOR; if the agency fails to meaningfully respond to relevant points, that omission can be the basis for judicial challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and timeliness standard for agency consideration and response
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA requires the rulemaking agency to consider all relevant and timely comments. The agency is only required to respond to comments that are directed at the proposed regulations or procedures followed (i.e., relevant) and that are received during the applicable comment period (i.e., timely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comments are both directed at the substance or procedures of the proposal and submitted within the applicable period; otherwise the agency may lawfully ignore them or need not respond.
